true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The second method definition overwrites the width/height form

Ruby does not overload methods by argument list, so this definition replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition immediately above it. Existing callers using the previously supported width/height arguments will now pass the height as `opts` or raise an argument error, breaking those callers. Use a single method that handles both forms or update all callers.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The client-side limit now ignores configured attachment sizes

This fixed 10 MB limit is applied to both images and attachments, bypassing the configured per-type limits. For example, installations that allow attachments larger than 10 MB will have valid uploads rejected in the browser; installations with a lower attachment limit will let users submit files the server then rejects. Keep attachment validation tied to its configured limit.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsizing can permanently discard animation frames

When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, `OptimizedImage` uses its non-animated conversion path, which reads only `from[0]`. Because this call uses the same path for input and output, an oversized animated GIF is replaced with a still image and its remaining frames are lost. Thumbnail settings should not silently destroy animation in the uploaded file.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize the request hostname before matching

The query lowercases the stored host but compares it to the request host unchanged, so a valid referer such as `http://EXAMPLE.COM` will not match a configured `example.com`. Also, `URI(host).host` omits the port, while the model accepts and stores hosts such as `example.com:8080`, so those configured entries can never match. Normalize case and handle ports consistently on both sides.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize legacy host values during migration

This inserts each legacy value verbatim, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s normalization callback. Existing allowed-host entries may include a scheme or path, both of which the old configuration supported; `record_for_host` later compares against `URI(...).host`, which contains only the bare hostname. Those migrated entries will never match, so previously allowed sites lose embedding access. Strip schemes and paths before inserting.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle an unset legacy embedding category

The legacy `embed_category` setting is optional, so this query can return no rows when the setting is blank, unset, or names a category that no longer exists. Indexing `[0]['id']` then raises before the fallback below can run, preventing the migration and blocking upgrades for those sites. Check for a matching row before reading it and use the uncategorized category when none exists.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

false_positives.candidate:
Accept valid domains with longer top-level domains

The validation restricts the final domain label to 2–5 letters, rejecting valid hostnames with longer top-level domains, such as `example.museum` or `example.photography`. Administrators cannot add these otherwise valid embedding hosts.

Do not use affected-row count to test a SELECT result

`cmd_tuples` reports rows affected by a command, not rows returned by this SELECT, so it is zero even when the legacy host setting exists. The migration therefore skips copying the host list and then deletes the original settings at line 31, permanently losing the configured allowlist. Check the result's returned-row count instead.

Preserve unresolved plural foreign keys

This branch always replaces a `*_ids` field and deletes it, even when `_lookupSubType` cannot find the corresponding embedded object and returns `undefined`. If a REST-serialized payload includes IDs but omits the plural collection or an individual referenced item, the model loses the IDs and receives a relationship array containing `undefined`. Preserve the original IDs unless the related objects were actually resolved.

false_negatives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Saving the level directly lets auto-tracking undo the unsubscribe

This direct save bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which stamps `notifications_changed_at` and sets `notifications_reason_id` to `user_changed` when a notification level is explicitly changed. Email recipients can have a topic-user row with a nil reason; `update_last_read` treats that row as eligible for automatic tracking and can raise the level back to `tracking` after the user reads enough of the topic. Use the normal notification-level update path so the user's explicit preference is preserved.

The GET unsubscribe endpoint changes user state

This action is reached through a GET route but changes the current user's notification preference before returning the page. Because GET requests do not require a CSRF token, a cross-site link or navigation can trigger the change whenever the user has an active Discourse session. Keep GET read-only and require an explicit CSRF-protected action to apply the preference.

The route name does not match the added template path

This declares a top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route, whose conventional template lookup is for `topic-unsubscribe`; the added template is `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which corresponds to a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route. There is no explicit template-name override, so visiting this route will not render the unsubscribe page. Nest the route under `topic` or provide a template matching the declared route name.

Unsubscribe does not mute users who are tracking or watching

When a user's notification level is `tracking` or `watching`, this branch lowers it only to `regular`. Regular topics can still send notifications for replies and mentions, so the page's promise to stop notifications is not met. Set the level to `muted` for every unsubscribe request, regardless of the starting level.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validation side effects count each signup attempt more than once

`BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments match statistics, but it is called from a validator, which can run multiple times for one operation. In particular, `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again; a matching address therefore increments `match_count` twice for one signup attempt. Keep validation side-effect-free and record a match once at the submission boundary.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Exact email lookup lets casing changes bypass the blocklist

This lookup compares the submitted address verbatim with the stored address, and signup does not normalize the email before validation. Because email domains are case-insensitive, a user can submit the same address with different domain casing (for example, `bad@SPAMCLUB.COM` instead of `bad@spamclub.com`) and avoid the blocklist match. Normalize both stored and submitted addresses before comparing them.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Concurrent matches can lose counter increments

The counter is updated with a read-modify-save sequence. If two signup validations load the same row before either saves, both can write the same incremented value, losing one match from `match_count`. Use an atomic database increment (and update the timestamp atomically) or lock the row.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
RSS items with only a description abort feed polling

A standard RSS item commonly provides its body in `<description>` rather than `content`; when SimpleRSS has no `content` value, calling `.scrub` on it raises `NoMethodError`. That aborts the poll before later items are processed, and this job has retries disabled. Fall back to the item's description (and handle items with neither field).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Raw HTML imports bypass post sanitization

Posts imported from RSS are assigned `cook_method: raw_html`, so this branch stores the feed's HTML directly as `cooked` instead of passing it through the normal rendering and sanitization pipeline. Feed content is unescaped before import and is rendered as HTML, so a feed publisher can inject scripts or event handlers that execute on forum pages with the forum's origin and user privileges. Sanitize imported HTML before it is stored or rendered.

Remote fetches can follow redirects to internal addresses

The embed URL's hostname is checked before this fetch, but `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects without rechecking the destination. An allowed-host URL that redirects to loopback, a private network address, or cloud metadata can therefore make the server fetch internal resources; the response is then passed into the import path. Restrict redirect targets and reject private or otherwise non-public resolved addresses.

The embed URL column truncates valid long URLs

A Rails `string` column defaults to `varchar(255)`, while valid embed URLs can exceed 255 characters, especially when they contain query parameters. Saving such an embed raises a database error inside the topic transaction, so the topic import is rolled back. Use a column type and index strategy that support the intended URL lengths.

The iframe height attribute is assigned an invalid value

`HTMLIFrameElement.height` reflects an integer-pixel HTML attribute, but this assigns a value such as `500px`. Browsers can treat that as invalid and use the default iframe height instead, leaving the embed clipped even after receiving a resize message. Assign the numeric pixel value or set `iframe.style.height`.

The throttle key can be left without an expiration

`SETNX` and `EXPIRE` are separate Redis operations. If the process stops or the second command fails after `SETNX` succeeds, the key remains indefinitely; subsequent non-staff retrieval attempts then treat the URL as recently retrieved and never fetch it. Set the key and TTL atomically, or remove the key when expiration setup fails.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
The legacy flexbox fallback may not keep the panel right-aligned

For browsers that use the `-webkit-box` or `-moz-box` fallback but do not support modern flexbox, `margin-left: auto` does not provide the modern flex auto-margin behavior that pushes the panel to the right. The previous `float: right` has also been removed, so the panel can sit beside the title rather than at the right edge.

The old Firefox flexbox fallback omits its alignment property

`flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` for older Firefox, but `align-items()` does not emit the corresponding `-moz-box-align`. In browsers using that fallback, requested vertical alignment (such as the header's `center`) is ignored and the items use the old box model's default alignment. Add the matching legacy property or remove the fallback.

The small-action button no longer floats to the right

Making `.small-action` a flex container causes its button child to ignore the existing `float: right`. Since `.small-action-desc` has no flex-grow, the button can sit directly beside the message instead of at the far right, changing the placement of the action control. Give the description flexible space or push the button to the end with a flex-compatible rule.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Website privacy restriction is bypassed by website_name

`website` is an untrusted attribute, so it is omitted for anonymous viewers of TL0 users when `restrict_user_fields?` applies. The newly serialized `website_name` is not in `untrusted_attributes`, and its inclusion method lacks the `?` used by the serializer's inclusion checks. It therefore still exposes the website host—and sometimes its path—in the user JSON, bypassing the existing privacy restriction.

true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Exact page-sized groups show a phantom page

`floor(user_count / limit) + 1` overcounts whenever the member count is an exact multiple of the page size. For example, 50 members at a limit of 50 are shown as 1/2, and Next loads an empty page. Use a ceiling-based page count instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Exact page-sized groups show a phantom page

`floor(user_count / limit) + 1` overcounts whenever the member count is an exact multiple of the page size. For example, 50 members at a limit of 50 are shown as 1/2, and Next loads an empty page. Use a ceiling-based page count instead.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

false_positives.candidate:
Removing the last member on a page leaves the list empty

After a member is removed, `removeMember` reloads the current page, but this offset is clamped using the model's pre-removal `user_count`. If the removed member was the only one on the last page, the requested offset is now at or past the new total, so the refresh returns no members and leaves the UI on an empty page. Adjust the offset after receiving the updated total, or move back a page when necessary.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Changing the site default locale can leave cached translations stale

The fallback chain depends on the current `SiteSetting.default_locale`, but the translation accelerator caches results using only the key, active locale, and backend identity. After the site default locale changes, a key missing from the active locale can continue returning the translation from the old default locale until its cache entry is evicted or the process restarts.

Fallback locales are loaded only for controller requests

This loads the fallback chain only in the controller locale filter. The translation accelerator loads only the active locale, and translations are loaded on demand, so a mailer or background job that sets a non-default locale and calls `I18n.t` without passing through this filter cannot find missing keys in the site-default or English locale. Such calls return missing translations instead of the configured fallback.

true_positives.golden_comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
This call does not match the inherited method signature

`UsernamePasswordForm` defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)`, and no zero-argument overload exists in its superclass. This invocation therefore fails Java compilation; pass the current user or add the intended overload.

true_positives.golden_comment: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Conditional passkeys are disabled before a user is identified

This helper returns false whenever `user` is null, but the initial login is precisely when a userless discoverable passkey must be offered. The calls that populate the form with WebAuthn challenge data are guarded by this helper, so normal unauthenticated logins through this form no longer get conditional passkey UI; passkey-only users cannot authenticate through this flow.

false_positives.candidate:
Clear setup events before asserting the first login

This test logs out after `registerDefaultUser()` but does not clear captured events before opening the login form. Setup can leave login events in the event collector, so the following `expectLogin()` may inspect a stale event instead of the passkey login. Clear the events after logout, as the neighboring tests do.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative QuerySet offsets are not supported by Django

This branch passes a negative start index to a Django QuerySet slice. Django raises `ValueError` for negative slice indices rather than treating them as offsets from the end, so an authorized request using the advertised negative-offset pagination path fails instead of returning a page. Implement reverse traversal without negative slicing, or reject negative offsets explicitly.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Optimized pagination cannot handle audit-log datetimes

The audit-log endpoint orders by `datetime`, so each item key here is a `datetime` object. Passing it to `math.floor` raises `TypeError` on the first non-empty page when `optimized_pagination=true` is used by an authorized administrator. The cursor conversion also returns the raw integer value rather than converting it back to a datetime, so subsequent-page filtering would fail too. Use the datetime key and cursor conversions from `DateTimePaginator`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative cursor offsets cause unsupported Django queryset slicing

When advanced features are enabled, a negative cursor offset is passed directly as the start of a queryset slice. Django querysets reject negative slice indices with `ValueError`; `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets, so a request containing such a cursor returns a server error rather than a pagination response or a client error.

When advanced features are enabled, a negative cursor offset is passed directly as the start of a queryset slice. Django querysets reject negative slice indices with `ValueError`; `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets, so a request containing such a cursor returns a server error rather than a pagination response or a client error.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime fields

The audit-log endpoint orders by `datetime`, but this implementation uses `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on the field value, which is a `datetime`; that raises `TypeError` when `build_cursor` processes a nonempty page. Its `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime, so subsequent-page filtering would fail as well. This paginator needs the datetime cursor encoding used by `DateTimePaginator`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

false_positives.candidate:
Changing the Redis key type breaks buffers created by the previous version

This changes `span-buf:s:*` keys from Redis sets to sorted sets without changing the key namespace or migrating existing keys. During a rollout, active keys written by the old version remain sets; `ZADD` here then fails with `WRONGTYPE` (and the Lua script also uses sorted-set commands on these keys). Consumers processing traces with such buffers will fail until the keys expire, stalling ingestion and potentially losing buffered spans.

Paginator-specific option is passed to the endpoint pagination helper

`enable_advanced_features` is an option on `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, but this call passes it to `self.paginate`. The endpoint pagination helper does not accept or forward this paginator-specific keyword, so an authorized administrator requesting `optimized_pagination=true` gets a `TypeError` instead of a response. Pass the option through the helper's supported mechanism or construct the paginator with it.

The eviction limit ignores the configured segment span limit

Eviction is hard-coded to 1000 here, while `SpansBuffer` exposes `max_segment_spans` as a configurable limit and previously enforced that value when loading segments. The new insertion-time cap no longer honors non-default values, so configurations expecting a lower cap can retain and emit substantially more spans than allowed, while higher configured limits are silently reduced.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Error-split dashboard queries use the original dataset for eligibility

`_get_event_stats` receives a `scoped_dataset`, but this check passes the outer `dataset` selected for the request. For a metrics-enhanced dashboard widget split into `ERROR_EVENTS`, the caller executes the error query against `discover` while the outer dataset remains a metrics dataset, so `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` rejects it and the split error count stays unupsampled. The eligibility check needs to reflect the dataset and query actually being executed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

false_positives.candidate:
Substring matching enables upsampling for non-error queries

This check matches `event.type:error` anywhere in the query, including negated filters such as `!event.type:error` and mixed queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. Those queries include non-error events, but the rewritten aggregation sums `sample_weight`, which is not defined for transactions. The result can undercount events or make the query fail; determine that the query positively restricts results to errors instead of searching for a substring.

The errors dataset uses an aggregation registered only for discover

This branch enables transformation for the `errors` dataset, causing `count()` to become `upsampled_count()`. The new function is registered only in `DiscoverDataset.function_converter` in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`; the errors dataset cannot resolve that function, so allowlisted requests using that dataset fail when the rewritten query is built. Register the function for the errors query path too, or avoid rewriting that dataset.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The feature-flagged table visualization receives no query results

When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch passes `columns={[]}` and a `tableData` object with empty `data`, `fields`, and `units` instead of using the current `result`. Consequently, dashboard table widgets in the flagged cohort render no columns or rows even when the query returned data.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reports without a valid age or timestamp pass validation

Both `age` and `timestamp` are optional, but there is no object-level check requiring exactly one, so a report containing neither is accepted and counted as valid. `age` also has no nonnegative minimum, and the mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness, allowing both fields to be present as zero. These invalid reports receive HTTP 200 and pollute the received-report metrics.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
Falsy custom cell output incorrectly falls back to the default renderer

The renderer contract says fallback occurs when a custom renderer returns `undefined`, but this truthiness check also treats valid outputs such as `null`, `false`, `0`, and an empty string as missing. A caller cannot intentionally render a blank cell or a falsy value; the default field renderer is shown instead.

Tabular rows cannot represent boolean field values

`TabularValueType` includes `boolean`, but `TabularRow` only permits numbers, strings, string arrays, and null. Callers therefore cannot type valid table data for boolean fields without a cast, undermining the new table API's type safety.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code consumption is not atomic

This read-modify-write can let concurrent login requests both validate the same backup code. Requests using different codes can also overwrite each other’s updates because each writes a stale copy of the entire encrypted list, restoring a code that was already consumed. This breaks the promised one-time-use guarantee and allows backup-code replay; consume codes with an atomic compare-and-swap or equivalent serialized update.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Password visibility toggle is no longer keyboard reachable

Setting `tabIndex={-1}` removes the show/hide password button from the Tab order for every `PasswordField`. Keyboard-only users can no longer focus or activate this control; keep it keyboard reachable.

The new backup-code login flow is not covered by an end-to-end test

The added test exercises displaying, downloading, and copying codes, but never attempts login with a backup code or verifies that a consumed code is rejected. The central authentication behavior—and its one-time-use contract—can therefore regress while this test still passes; add coverage for successful backup-code login and reuse rejection.

The setup password visibility toggle cannot reveal the password

This field passes `type="password"` to `PasswordField`. That component sets its visibility-dependent type before spreading the supplied props, so this fixed type overrides the component’s `text` type when the eye toggle is clicked. Remove the explicit type or change the component so the toggle can reveal the password.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Meet fallback throws when no destination calendar is configured

When `destinationCalendar` is null or empty, destructuring leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined, so accessing `.integration` throws before the booking can be created. This is the very case the fallback is meant to handle: a Google Meet location with no Google Calendar should switch to Cal Video rather than fail the booking.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google update and delete cannot resolve a destination when the reference has no external ID

When `externalCalendarId` is null or undefined, this lookup compares each real calendar ID to that same nullish value and finds nothing. Updates then send no calendar ID; deletes fall back to `primary` (the same faulty lookup appears at line 317), so an event in the configured destination can remain orphaned after cancellation. This affects callers or older references without an external calendar ID.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organizations created without team billing no longer receive their slug

This reverses the previous condition: when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, the organization is now created without a `slug`; when it is true, the slug is assigned immediately as well as recorded as `requestedSlug`. In the non-billing configuration, organizations therefore lack the slug needed for their organization URL.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
Co-host calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar

The event is initialized with `destinationCalendar: null` when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar. Optional-chaining this push then does nothing, even when `teamDestinationCalendars` contains calendars for collective co-hosts. Event creation consequently receives no co-host destinations, so those hosts do not get calendar entries.

Google ignores configured destinations without a credential ID

When a destination has an external ID but no `credentialId`, the event manager still supports it by selecting credentials by integration type. This lookup then finds no match and falls back to `primary`, so creation ignores the configured destination calendar and may write to the wrong calendar.

Google update and delete cannot resolve a destination when the reference has no external ID

When `externalCalendarId` is null or undefined, this lookup compares each real calendar ID to that same nullish value and finds nothing. Updates then send no calendar ID; deletes fall back to `primary` (the same faulty lookup appears at line 317), so an event in the configured destination can remain orphaned after cancellation. This affects callers or older references without an external calendar ID.

Lark creates every host's event in the first destination calendar

`EventManager` calls calendar creation once per destination using that destination's credential, but this method always selects `event.destinationCalendar[0]` and ignores the supplied credential ID. For a collective booking with multiple Lark credentials, later calls use the first host's calendar ID with another host's credentials, causing creation to fail or target the wrong calendar.

Only the first collective destination calendar is persisted for pending bookings

This relation stores only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]`, so the other hosts' destinations exist only in the in-memory event. For bookings awaiting confirmation or payment, later confirmation flows rebuild the event from the booking's single destination-calendar relation and the organizer's calendar; they cannot recover the co-host destinations. Those hosts therefore never receive calendar entries for these bookings.

Recurring cancellation still processes only the first calendar reference

In the recurring-booking path, each future booking is reduced to its first calendar reference, and the code then uses the organizer's credentials rather than the credential for each reference. Collective bookings now have multiple references, including co-host calendars, so canceling all remaining instances can leave those calendar copies in place or attempt deletion through the wrong account.

Video booking references lose their credential ID

This now sets `credentialId` to `undefined` for every non-calendar result, discarding the video result's credential ID. Cancellation code only deletes a video meeting when its booking reference has a credential ID, so meetings created through video integrations can remain active after their booking is canceled.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The minimum token schema does not capture arbitrary expiry fields

`z.string().toString()` is evaluated as a literal property name, not a wildcard key, and the same applies to the optional property on line 10. Consequently, normal fields such as `expires_in` or `expiry_date` are not validated or retained by this `z.object` (which strips unrecognized properties); depending on the computed keys, responses may also fail parsing. With credential syncing enabled, token refreshes across the affected apps therefore fail or lose their expiry data.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The SafeParse wrapper is saved as the Google credential key

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the result of `safeParse`, which has the shape `{ success, data }`, but this line stores that whole result as `credential.key` instead of its `.data`. After a token refresh, the next Google auth initialization parses this wrapper as a Google credential and fails, leaving the integration unusable.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Bigin sends a credential row ID as the user ID

The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is used as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`, the ID of the credential row, rather than the owning user's ID. The sync endpoint will look up the wrong user (or fail to find one), so Bigin token refreshes cannot reliably retrieve the correct user's credentials.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The Salesforce connection uses the pre-refresh access token

The newly added code obtains and stores a refreshed token, but the connection is then constructed with `credentialKey.access_token`, which came from the original credential and was not updated with `accessTokenParsed.data`. When the original token is expired, Salesforce API calls therefore use the expired token despite the successful refresh.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

false_positives.candidate:
Concurrent initial webhooks can create duplicate credentials

The lookup at line 62 and the create here are separate, non-atomic operations. If two deliveries for the same user and app arrive before either creates its row, both observe no credential and insert one. This leaves duplicate credentials, after which consumers using `findFirst` may select an arbitrary copy.

Salesforce refresh bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint

This refresh path calls Salesforce directly instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`. When credential syncing is configured, Salesforce still refreshes against Cal.com's Salesforce app rather than the self-hosted platform's source of truth, so the advertised sync behavior does not work for Salesforce.

The new credential update references an unimported Prisma client

This file does not import or otherwise declare `prisma`, but the newly added refresh code calls `prisma.credential.update`. TypeScript compilation fails with an unresolved `prisma` name, preventing the app-store package or application from building.

The synced Teams token is immediately treated as expired

The sync endpoint is expected to return an access token and expiry date, but the refresh handling later derives `expiry_date` solely from `expires_in` and overwrites it with `Date.now()` when `expires_in` is absent. The next `getToken` call sees that timestamp as expired and calls the sync endpoint again, causing repeated refresh requests and potentially rate-limiting the integration.

Webex rejects the documented minimal sync response

The sync endpoint is documented to return only an access token and expiry date, but the response is passed on to `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` at line 88, which also requires `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`. A response following the stated sync contract fails validation, so Webex refreshes fail and the integration cannot use synced credentials.

Zoom sync uses a different slug from the stored app credential

The refresh request identifies Zoom as `zoomvideo`, while Zoom credentials are stored with `appId: "zoom"` (as shown by the callback). The receiving sync endpoint uses `appSlug` to identify the app, so it cannot reliably match this request to the Zoom credential.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Mixed-case addresses bypass the guest email blocklist

Blocklist entries are lowercased, but the submitted guest address is compared without normalization. A mixed- or uppercase spelling of a blocked address therefore passes the filter and is added to the booking. Normalize the submitted address before checking the blocklist.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team access requires both admin and owner roles

This condition grants the team path only when both checks return true. Team admins who are not owners—and owners not recognized as admins—are therefore denied access, even though the intent appears to allow either role. Use an OR between the checks.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Email classification uses requested guests rather than guests actually added

The handler filters existing attendees out of uniqueGuests, but passes the original guests array to sendAddGuestsEmails. If a request contains both an existing attendee and a new address, the existing attendee is still classified as newly added and receives an AttendeeScheduledEmail, causing a duplicate booking confirmation or calendar invite. Pass uniqueGuests so notification types reflect the attendees actually inserted.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The server does not enforce unique guest addresses

The input schema checks only email syntax, and this filter checks each value only against the attendees loaded before the request. Repeated addresses in the request, or case variants of an existing address, can all pass and be sent to createMany. This can create duplicate attendee records (or make the mutation fail if a database constraint rejects them); enforce uniqueness on normalized addresses server-side.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

false_positives.candidate:
Calendar updates use the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's

This procedure allows an existing attendee to add guests, but it constructs EventManager with credentials for ctx.user. For an attendee caller, those are not the credentials for the organizer-owned calendar, so updating that calendar's attendee list can fail or be skipped. The attendee rows are already committed before this call, and a failure also prevents the email step, leaving guests persisted without the expected calendar update or notifications.

The guest list has no size limit despite per-attendee fan-out

This array is unbounded, and each accepted address creates an attendee row and adds work for calendar synchronization and email delivery. An authorized booking participant can submit thousands of unique addresses in one request, causing large database writes and a correspondingly large email fan-out. Enforce a reasonable maximum batch size (and consider rate limiting).

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Increment retryCount atomically

Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value loaded before the SMS call. If two cron invocations process the same reminder concurrently, they can both read the same count and overwrite it with the same next value. The failed attempts are then counted as one, so the reminder can be retried more than twice instead of being removed at the intended limit. Use Prisma's atomic `increment` update in both failure paths.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
Execute org and team authorization SQL in integration tests

The only database-backed query here uses user scope, which does not exercise the new `ANY(...)` array predicates. The org/team tests only compare `Prisma.Sql` fragments, so they will not catch invalid PostgreSQL array binding or incorrect authorization results when those predicates execute. Add database-backed queries covering org and team scopes.

Preserve or migrate the public `findMany` API

This change removes the service’s public `findMany` method and replaces it with a condition builder, but no production call sites are migrated in this PR. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany(...)` will no longer type-check, so the application cannot build until those callers are updated or a compatible method is retained.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The existing-URL update only works with BSD sed

`sed -i ''` uses BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU/Linux, when `.env` already contains `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`, this command treats the empty argument as a file operand and fails to update the value; because the script does not stop on that failure, it can still print that the file was updated. Use a portable in-place edit or branch on the platform.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

false_positives.candidate:
Deleting cache leaves the displayed status stale

The delete mutation only invokes an optional `onSuccess` callback and does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. When no callback is provided, the mounted query retains the deleted cache’s `cacheUpdatedAt`, so the dropdown continues to report cached data and offer deletion after the operation succeeded. Invalidate or refetch the connected-calendars query after deletion.

Legacy cache rows are reported as updated at migration time

Adding this column with `DEFAULT NOW()` assigns the migration timestamp to every existing cache row. The UI presents `updatedAt` as the cache’s last-updated time, so all pre-existing caches appear freshly updated on deployment even when their contents are older. Backfill a timestamp derived from the existing cache metadata, or avoid presenting the migration-time value as the actual update time.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Immediate cancellations still fill SendGrid's pending-cancellation limit

When `immediateDelete` is true, this sends the SendGrid cancel request immediately and returns without setting `cancelled=true`. Rescheduling uses this path, as do workflow/step deletion, so far-future sends remain in SendGrid's pending-cancellation queue until their scheduled dates—the limit of 100 that this PR is intended to avoid can still be reached. Once reached, later cancellations can fail and reminders may be sent. If the request fails, the error is swallowed and the cron has no `cancelled` flag to retry. These cancellations need to use the deferred cancellation flow or otherwise ensure they are cleaned up and retried.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
One failed cancellation aborts the rest of the cron batch

The `try` covers the entire loop, so a single failed SendGrid request exits the loop and skips every later cancelled reminder in the batch. Those reminders remain pending at SendGrid; if one becomes due before the next cron run, the initial cleanup at lines 34–41 deletes its database row before it can be retried, and the email can be sent. Handle failures per reminder or ensure due cancelled reminders are processed before cleanup.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reschedule does not wait for calendar deletion

`forEach` discards the promises returned by its async callbacks. Since `getCalendar` now requires an asynchronous import, the callback can still be waiting for the app module when this function finishes sending the email and returns; the old calendar event can therefore remain in place after rescheduling, and callback failures will not be caught by the surrounding `try/catch`. Await the callbacks, for example with `Promise.all`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

false_positives.candidate:
All app imports are still started eagerly

Each `import()` is evaluated while this object is constructed, so importing the app-store barrel immediately starts loading every app module, even when the caller needs only one. This does not provide on-demand loading and means a cold request that first touches the app store can still pay for loading and evaluating all app packages.

Recurring cancellation can finish before calendar deletions are tracked

The async callback is not awaited by `forEach`. It only adds a deletion to `apiDeletes` after awaiting both `getCalendar` and `deleteEvent`, while the outer handler can reach its later `Promise.all` before either finishes. The handler may then delete booking references and report cancellation without deleting the external recurring calendar events; any later callback failure also escapes the surrounding flow.

Reschedule does not wait for integration deletions

`forEach` discards the promises returned by its async callbacks. The mutation can proceed to send the reschedule email and return while a callback is still awaiting `getCalendar`, leaving the old calendar event undeleted when the request completes. Errors from those callbacks are also not propagated. Await the callbacks, for example with `Promise.all`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hour check ignores the event end time

`end` is calculated identically to `start`, so the check only verifies that the slot begins within a working-hour interval. A fixed host whose hours end at 10:00 can consequently be treated as available for a 09:30 slot lasting 60 minutes, even though the event ends at 10:30. Check the slot's actual end against the interval end.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

false_positives.candidate:
Date overrides bypass busy-time checks

When a slot falls within a date override, this returns `true` before the subsequent `busy.every` check. Existing bookings and calendar events are still reported in `busy`, so a host can be shown as available during an override despite already being booked, allowing a double booking. An override should replace regular working hours, not ignore busy times.

Multiple override windows reject each other

The `.find` callback returns a truthy value when the slot is outside the current override window, which immediately marks the slot unavailable without checking later windows. For example, with overrides 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a slot in either window is rejected because it falls outside the other one. Check whether the slot fits any window for that date instead.

Slots only need to overlap an override to be accepted

These checks reject slots wholly before or after an override, but accept any slot that overlaps it. For example, a 09:30–10:30 slot passes a 10:00–11:00 override even though it starts outside the host's availability. This can incorrectly count a fixed host as available for a slot generated from another host; require the entire slot to fit within the override.

Split working-hour windows make slots unavailable

This rejects a slot if `.find` finds any working-hour interval that does not contain it, rather than rejecting only when no interval contains it. With 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 hours, a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the second interval. Hosts with multiple windows on a day can therefore lose their availability.

Timezone conversion drops date changes across midnight

The timezone adjustment can move an override to the previous or next day, but this code keeps only its hour and minute and later anchors those to the unshifted invitee day. The active-override filter also selects overrides using the unshifted start date. For example, an override at 00:30 in UTC+5:30 maps to 19:00 on the prior UTC day, but is selected and placed on the original date for a UTC invitee. Availability near timezone day boundaries is therefore missing or shown on the wrong day.

Timezone test can pass when expected slots are missing

This assertion uses `toHaveTimeSlots`, whose implementation iterates the actual slots and compares each with the expected slot at that index. If the result contains only a matching prefix—for example, one of the four expected slots—the matcher still passes. The new timezone regression test therefore does not ensure that all expected slots are returned.

This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.

Reject non-positive flusher process limits

false_positives.candidate:
A missing Kafka offset can permanently block commits

The tracker requires every integer offset between `start` and `max_offset` to have been received. Kafka consumers can legitimately observe gaps, for example when compacted or aborted records are not returned. The first such gap makes this loop stop advancing even when every delivered message is complete; later messages then remain uncommitted and may be replayed indefinitely. Track the order of observed messages rather than requiring numeric adjacency.

A negative worker count creates a pool that commits without processing

`max_workers` is accepted as an unrestricted integer, and a negative value is truthy, so it produces a negative `num_queues` and starts no workers. Submissions then index an empty queue list; the strategy catches that error and marks the message offset complete, so results can be committed without processing. Reject non-positive worker counts before creating the pool.

Closing a strategy permanently shuts down the shared queue pool

`queue_pool` is owned by `ResultsStrategyFactory` and reused by each `create_with_partitions` call, but closing one strategy shuts it down. When Arroyo recreates a strategy after a partition-assignment change, the factory reuses this non-None pool with stopped workers and shut-down queues. Subsequent submissions fail, and `submit()` treats those failures as completed offsets, allowing results to be committed without processing. Keep the shared pool alive across strategy instances, or create and manage a separate pool per strategy.

Processing failures are marked complete and committed

This runs in `finally`, so an exception from `result_processor` still removes the offset from the outstanding set. The commit loop can then advance past a result that was never processed; failures swallowed by `ResultProcessor.__call__` have the same outcome. Do not mark an offset complete until processing succeeds or the message is explicitly routed to a failure-handling path.

Queue shutdown APIs are unavailable before Python 3.13

`Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were added in Python 3.13. On supported Python runtimes before 3.13, this call raises `AttributeError` and is swallowed; workers remain blocked in `get()`, and `shutdown()` then waits up to five seconds per worker before leaving daemon threads behind. Use a shutdown mechanism compatible with the project's minimum Python version or require Python 3.13+.

The queues are unbounded and provide no backpressure

`queue.Queue()` defaults to an unlimited size, and `submit()` can keep adding work without waiting for workers. If Kafka intake outpaces processing, queued `WorkItem`s and their message payloads can grow without limit until the consumer runs out of memory. Use bounded queues and propagate saturation back to polling or another explicit backpressure mechanism.

true_positives.golden_comment: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. Denial key can collide for different resource and folder pairs

Since dashboard and folder UIDs can contain underscores, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce the same key. A denial for the first check then short-circuits the second check even if that resource is allowed, for up to the cache TTL. Encode the components unambiguously, such as with length prefixes.

The reverse can also deny an anonymous user who has permission. Include the identity type in the denial key to prevent one identity’s decision from affecting another.

Since MySQL timestamps are stored at second precision, a request on another instance in the same second with the same IP and user agent can leave every updated column unchanged and incorrectly return `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, rejecting an already-registered device when the cap is full. The new configuration option is not documented

Max-count cleanup can delete annotations that moved into the retained set

The IDs are selected using the max-count offset, then deleted in a separate statement without rechecking their rank. If another request deletes a newer annotation between those statements, a selected ID can move into the set that should be retained but will still be deleted. For example, with a max count of 1, cleanup selects the older of two annotations; if a user deletes the newer one before this delete, cleanup then removes the only remaining annotation.

false_positives.candidate:
Background legacy writes inherit the request context

`WithTimeoutCause` creates a child of the incoming request context; it does not detach cancellation. The API server cancels that context when the request handler returns, which happens immediately after this method returns, so the legacy write can be canceled before it completes. The same pattern is used for delete, update, and delete-collection at lines 110, 135, and 163. The unified write is still reported as successful, leaving legacy storage unsynchronized.

Destroy does not wait for in-flight legacy writes

The asynchronous writes are not tracked, but `Destroy` immediately destroys both backends. If shutdown calls `Destroy` while a legacy write is still running, the backend can be closed underneath that write and the shadow write can be lost. Track and drain pending writes, or otherwise ensure the legacy backend remains available until they finish.

Independent goroutines can apply mutations to legacy out of order

Every successful mutation starts an independent goroutine, with no per-resource ordering or queue. For example, a delete can reach legacy before an earlier create, return not found, and then the delayed create can leave the supposedly deleted object in legacy; an update can similarly arrive before its create. These legacy errors are not retried, so the stores can remain divergent.

Legacy updates are recomputed against a potentially divergent object

The legacy update receives the original `objInfo`, so it computes the update independently against the legacy object's current state. During dual writing, that state can differ from unified storage; patches, defaults, or other update logic can therefore produce a legacy object different from the object successfully written to unified storage. The previous implementation passed the unified update result to legacy through an update wrapper, avoiding this divergence.

Recheck the cache after acquiring the write lock

A burst of initial requests therefore serializes repeated file reads and JSON decoding; if a later read fails, it can also replace the successfully populated cache with nil. The provider contract treats null as no organization filter for `ORG_ONLY`/`ALL`, but treats any non-null ID—including an empty string—as a specific organization filter. false_positives.candidate:
Processing failures are marked complete and committed

This runs in `finally`, so an exception from `result_processor` still removes the offset from the outstanding set. The commit loop can then advance past a result that was never processed; failures swallowed by `ResultProcessor.__call__` have the same outcome. Do not mark an offset complete until processing succeeds or the message is explicitly routed to a failure-handling path.

Closing a strategy permanently shuts down the shared queue pool

`queue_pool` is owned by `ResultsStrategyFactory` and reused by each `create_with_partitions` call, but closing one strategy shuts it down. When Arroyo recreates a strategy after a partition-assignment change, the factory reuses this non-None pool with stopped workers and shut-down queues. Subsequent submissions fail, and `submit()` treats those failures as completed offsets, allowing results to be committed without processing. Keep the shared pool alive across strategy instances, or create and manage a separate pool per strategy.

A missing Kafka offset can permanently block commits

The tracker requires every integer offset between `start` and `max_offset` to have been received. Kafka consumers can legitimately observe gaps, for example when compacted or aborted records are not returned. The first such gap makes this loop stop advancing even when every delivered message is complete; later messages then remain uncommitted and may be replayed indefinitely. Track the order of observed messages rather than requiring numeric adjacency.

The queues are unbounded and provide no backpressure

`queue.Queue()` defaults to an unlimited size, and `submit()` can keep adding work without waiting for workers. If Kafka intake outpaces processing, queued `WorkItem`s and their message payloads can grow without limit until the consumer runs out of memory. Use bounded queues and propagate saturation back to polling or another explicit backpressure mechanism.

Queue shutdown APIs are unavailable before Python 3.13

`Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were added in Python 3.13. On supported Python runtimes before 3.13, this call raises `AttributeError` and is swallowed; workers remain blocked in `get()`, and `shutdown()` then waits up to five seconds per worker before leaving daemon threads behind. Use a shutdown mechanism compatible with the project's minimum Python version or require Python 3.13+.

A negative worker count creates a pool that commits without processing

`max_workers` is accepted as an unrestricted integer, and a negative value is truthy, so it produces a negative `num_queues` and starts no workers. Submissions then index an empty queue list; the strategy catches that error and marks the message offset complete, so results can be committed without processing. Reject non-positive worker counts before creating the pool.
