This lookup compares the submitted address verbatim with the stored address, and signup does not normalize the email before validation. Because email domains are case-insensitive, a user can submit the same address with different domain casing (for example, `bad@SPAMCLUB.COM` instead of `bad@spamclub.com`) and avoid the blocklist match. Normalize both stored and submitted addresses before comparing them.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same bug: the email blocklist lookup is case-sensitive, which allows users to bypass the block by altering the casing of the email address.

false_positives.candidate:
Concurrent matches can lose counter increments

The counter is updated with a read-modify-save sequence. If two signup validations load the same row before either saves, both can write the same incremented value, losing one match from `match_count`. Use an atomic database increment (and update the timestamp atomically) or lock the row.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
The small-action button no longer floats to the right

Making `.small-action` a flex container causes its button child to ignore the existing `float: right`. Since `.small-action-desc` has no flex-grow, the button can sit directly beside the message instead of at the far right, changing the placement of the action control. Give the description flexible space or push the button to the end with a flex-compatible rule.

The legacy flexbox fallback may not keep the panel right-aligned

For browsers that use the `-webkit-box` or `-moz-box` fallback but do not support modern flexbox, `margin-left: auto` does not provide the modern flex auto-margin behavior that pushes the panel to the right. The previous `float: right` has also been removed, so the panel can sit beside the title rather than at the right edge.

The old Firefox flexbox fallback omits its alignment property

`flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` for older Firefox, but `align-items()` does not emit the corresponding `-moz-box-align`. In browsers using that fallback, requested vertical alignment (such as the header's `center`) is ignored and the items use the old box model's default alignment. Add the matching legacy property or remove the fallback.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Website privacy restriction is bypassed by website_name

`website` is an untrusted attribute, so it is omitted for anonymous viewers of TL0 users when `restrict_user_fields?` applies. The newly serialized `website_name` is not in `untrusted_attributes`, and its inclusion method lacks the `?` used by the serializer's inclusion checks. It therefore still exposes the website host—and sometimes its path—in the user JSON, bypassing the existing privacy restriction.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue explicitly identifies the primary bug mentioned in the golden comment: that the `include_website_name` method is missing the required `?` suffix for serializer inclusion checks, causing `website_name` to be improperly included instead of conditionally omitted.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
RSS items with only a description abort feed polling

A standard RSS item commonly provides its body in `<description>` rather than `content`; when SimpleRSS has no `content` value, calling `.scrub` on it raises `NoMethodError`. That aborts the poll before later items are processed, and this job has retries disabled. Fall back to the item's description (and handle items with neither field).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue accurately identifies the exact same bug as the golden comment: calling `.scrub` on `content` when it is nil will cause an error for RSS feeds that only provide a `description`, and suggests falling back to `description`.

false_positives.candidate:
Raw HTML imports bypass post sanitization

Posts imported from RSS are assigned `cook_method: raw_html`, so this branch stores the feed's HTML directly as `cooked` instead of passing it through the normal rendering and sanitization pipeline. Feed content is unescaped before import and is rendered as HTML, so a feed publisher can inject scripts or event handlers that execute on forum pages with the forum's origin and user privileges. Sanitize imported HTML before it is stored or rendered.

Remote fetches can follow redirects to internal addresses

The embed URL's hostname is checked before this fetch, but `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects without rechecking the destination. An allowed-host URL that redirects to loopback, a private network address, or cloud metadata can therefore make the server fetch internal resources; the response is then passed into the import path. Restrict redirect targets and reject private or otherwise non-public resolved addresses.

The iframe height attribute is assigned an invalid value

`HTMLIFrameElement.height` reflects an integer-pixel HTML attribute, but this assigns a value such as `500px`. Browsers can treat that as invalid and use the default iframe height instead, leaving the embed clipped even after receiving a resize message. Assign the numeric pixel value or set `iframe.style.height`.

The embed URL column truncates valid long URLs

A Rails `string` column defaults to `varchar(255)`, while valid embed URLs can exceed 255 characters, especially when they contain query parameters. Saving such an embed raises a database error inside the topic transaction, so the topic import is rolled back. Use a column type and index strategy that support the intended URL lengths.

The throttle key can be left without an expiration

`SETNX` and `EXPIRE` are separate Redis operations. If the process stops or the second command fails after `SETNX` succeeds, the key remains indefinitely; subsequent non-staff retrieval attempts then treat the URL as recently retrieved and never fetch it. Set the key and TTL atomically, or remove the key when expiration setup fails.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The second method definition overwrites the width/height form

Ruby does not overload methods by argument list, so this definition replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition immediately above it. Existing callers using the previously supported width/height arguments will now pass the height as `opts` or raise an argument error, breaking those callers. Use a single method that handles both forms or update all callers.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same issue: the `downsize` method is defined twice with different argument signatures, and because Ruby does not support method overloading, the second definition overwrites the first one, breaking callers that use the separate `max_width` and `max_height` parameters.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The client-side limit now ignores configured attachment sizes

This fixed 10 MB limit is applied to both images and attachments, bypassing the configured per-type limits. For example, installations that allow attachments larger than 10 MB will have valid uploads rejected in the browser; installations with a lower attachment limit will let users submit files the server then rejects. Keep attachment validation tied to its configured limit.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same problem: hardcoding the file size limit to 10MB ignores the configured per-type size settings, causing client-side validation to diverge from server-side limits.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsizing can permanently discard animation frames

When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, `OptimizedImage` uses its non-animated conversion path, which reads only `from[0]`. Because this call uses the same path for input and output, an oversized animated GIF is replaced with a still image and its remaining frames are lost. Thumbnail settings should not silently destroy animation in the uploaded file.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Unsubscribe does not mute users who are tracking or watching

When a user's notification level is `tracking` or `watching`, this branch lowers it only to `regular`. Regular topics can still send notifications for replies and mentions, so the page's promise to stop notifications is not met. Set the level to `muted` for every unsubscribe request, regardless of the starting level.

Saving the level directly lets auto-tracking undo the unsubscribe

This direct save bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which stamps `notifications_changed_at` and sets `notifications_reason_id` to `user_changed` when a notification level is explicitly changed. Email recipients can have a topic-user row with a nil reason; `update_last_read` treats that row as eligible for automatic tracking and can raise the level back to `tracking` after the user reads enough of the topic. Use the normal notification-level update path so the user's explicit preference is preserved.

The GET unsubscribe endpoint changes user state

This action is reached through a GET route but changes the current user's notification preference before returning the page. Because GET requests do not require a CSRF token, a cross-site link or navigation can trigger the change whenever the user has an active Discourse session. Keep GET read-only and require an explicit CSRF-protected action to apply the preference.

The route name does not match the added template path

This declares a top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route, whose conventional template lookup is for `topic-unsubscribe`; the added template is `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which corresponds to a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route. There is no explicit template-name override, so visiting this route will not render the unsubscribe page. Nest the route under `topic` or provide a template matching the declared route name.

Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

true_positives.matched_candidate:
The existing-URL update only works with BSD sed

`sed -i ''` uses BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU/Linux, when `.env` already contains `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`, this command treats the empty argument as a file operand and fails to update the value; because the script does not stop on that failure, it can still print that the file was updated. Use a portable in-place edit or branch on the platform.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: using the macOS/BSD-specific `sed -i ''` syntax, which will fail on Linux/GNU systems.

false_positives.candidate:
Deleting cache leaves the displayed status stale

The delete mutation only invokes an optional `onSuccess` callback and does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. When no callback is provided, the mounted query retains the deleted cache’s `cacheUpdatedAt`, so the dropdown continues to report cached data and offer deletion after the operation succeeded. Invalidate or refetch the connected-calendars query after deletion.

Legacy cache rows are reported as updated at migration time

Adding this column with `DEFAULT NOW()` assigns the migration timestamp to every existing cache row. The UI presents `updatedAt` as the cache’s last-updated time, so all pre-existing caches appear freshly updated on deployment even when their contents are older. Backfill a timestamp derived from the existing cache metadata, or avoid presenting the migration-time value as the actual update time.

This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hour check ignores the event end time

`end` is calculated identically to `start`, so the check only verifies that the slot begins within a working-hour interval. A fixed host whose hours end at 10:00 can consequently be treated as available for a 09:30 slot lasting 60 minutes, even though the event ends at 10:30. Check the slot's actual end against the interval end.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same bug: the `end` time is being calculated using the start time (`slotStartTime`), causing the working-hour check to ignore the actual end time of the slot/event.

false_positives.candidate:
Date overrides bypass busy-time checks

When a slot falls within a date override, this returns `true` before the subsequent `busy.every` check. Existing bookings and calendar events are still reported in `busy`, so a host can be shown as available during an override despite already being booked, allowing a double booking. An override should replace regular working hours, not ignore busy times.

Multiple override windows reject each other

The `.find` callback returns a truthy value when the slot is outside the current override window, which immediately marks the slot unavailable without checking later windows. For example, with overrides 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a slot in either window is rejected because it falls outside the other one. Check whether the slot fits any window for that date instead.

Slots only need to overlap an override to be accepted

These checks reject slots wholly before or after an override, but accept any slot that overlaps it. For example, a 09:30–10:30 slot passes a 10:00–11:00 override even though it starts outside the host's availability. This can incorrectly count a fixed host as available for a slot generated from another host; require the entire slot to fit within the override.

Split working-hour windows make slots unavailable

This rejects a slot if `.find` finds any working-hour interval that does not contain it, rather than rejecting only when no interval contains it. With 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 hours, a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the second interval. Hosts with multiple windows on a day can therefore lose their availability.

Timezone conversion drops date changes across midnight

The timezone adjustment can move an override to the previous or next day, but this code keeps only its hour and minute and later anchors those to the unshifted invitee day. The active-override filter also selects overrides using the unshifted start date. For example, an override at 00:30 in UTC+5:30 maps to 19:00 on the prior UTC day, but is selected and placed on the original date for a UTC invitee. Availability near timezone day boundaries is therefore missing or shown on the wrong day.

Timezone test can pass when expected slots are missing

This assertion uses `toHaveTimeSlots`, whose implementation iterates the actual slots and compares each with the expected slot at that index. If the result contains only a matching prefix—for example, one of the four expected slots—the matcher still passes. The new timezone regression test therefore does not ensure that all expected slots are returned.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Increment retryCount atomically

Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value loaded before the SMS call. If two cron invocations process the same reminder concurrently, they can both read the same count and overwrite it with the same next value. The failed attempts are then counted as one, so the reminder can be retried more than twice instead of being removed at the intended limit. Use Prisma's atomic `increment` update in both failure paths.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same concurrency/race condition issue with incrementing `reminder.retryCount` using in-memory addition (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) across both failure paths, and both suggest using Prisma's atomic `increment` operation instead.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

false_positives.candidate:
Preserve or migrate the public `findMany` API

This change removes the service’s public `findMany` method and replaces it with a condition builder, but no production call sites are migrated in this PR. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany(...)` will no longer type-check, so the application cannot build until those callers are updated or a compatible method is retained.

Execute org and team authorization SQL in integration tests

The only database-backed query here uses user scope, which does not exercise the new `ANY(...)` array predicates. The org/team tests only compare `Prisma.Sql` fragments, so they will not catch invalid PostgreSQL array binding or incorrect authorization results when those predicates execute. Add database-backed queries covering org and team scopes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The minimum token schema does not capture arbitrary expiry fields

`z.string().toString()` is evaluated as a literal property name, not a wildcard key, and the same applies to the optional property on line 10. Consequently, normal fields such as `expires_in` or `expiry_date` are not validated or retained by this `z.object` (which strips unrecognized properties); depending on the computed keys, responses may also fail parsing. With credential syncing enabled, token refreshes across the affected apps therefore fail or lose their expiry data.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug in `minimumTokenResponseSchema`: the misuse of computed property keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` inside a Zod `z.object()`, which is invalid/incorrect Zod syntax for defining dynamic/wildcard keys and breaks parsing.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The SafeParse wrapper is saved as the Google credential key

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the result of `safeParse`, which has the shape `{ success, data }`, but this line stores that whole result as `credential.key` instead of its `.data`. After a token refresh, the next Google auth initialization parses this wrapper as a Google credential and fails, leaving the integration unusable.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue point out the exact same bug: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `safeParse` wrapper object (`{ success, data }`), and the code erroneously persists this wrapper as the credential key instead of extracting the `.data` payload.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Bigin sends a credential row ID as the user ID

The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is used as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`, the ID of the credential row, rather than the owning user's ID. The sync endpoint will look up the wrong user (or fail to find one), so Bigin token refreshes cannot reliably retrieve the correct user's credentials.
true_positives.reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the exact same bug: `credentialId` is being passed to `refreshOAuthTokens` instead of the `userId`, which causes the sync functionality to look up the wrong user.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The Salesforce connection uses the pre-refresh access token

The newly added code obtains and stores a refreshed token, but the connection is then constructed with `credentialKey.access_token`, which came from the original credential and was not updated with `accessTokenParsed.data`. When the original token is expired, Salesforce API calls therefore use the expired token despite the successful refresh.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same bug: the Salesforce connection is constructed using the stale `credentialKey.access_token` instead of the newly refreshed token.

false_positives.candidate:
The new credential update references an unimported Prisma client

This file does not import or otherwise declare `prisma`, but the newly added refresh code calls `prisma.credential.update`. TypeScript compilation fails with an unresolved `prisma` name, preventing the app-store package or application from building.

Salesforce refresh bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint

This refresh path calls Salesforce directly instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`. When credential syncing is configured, Salesforce still refreshes against Cal.com's Salesforce app rather than the self-hosted platform's source of truth, so the advertised sync behavior does not work for Salesforce.

Webex rejects the documented minimal sync response

The sync endpoint is documented to return only an access token and expiry date, but the response is passed on to `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` at line 88, which also requires `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`. A response following the stated sync contract fails validation, so Webex refreshes fail and the integration cannot use synced credentials.

The synced Teams token is immediately treated as expired

The sync endpoint is expected to return an access token and expiry date, but the refresh handling later derives `expiry_date` solely from `expires_in` and overwrites it with `Date.now()` when `expires_in` is absent. The next `getToken` call sees that timestamp as expired and calls the sync endpoint again, causing repeated refresh requests and potentially rate-limiting the integration.

Zoom sync uses a different slug from the stored app credential

The refresh request identifies Zoom as `zoomvideo`, while Zoom credentials are stored with `appId: "zoom"` (as shown by the callback). The receiving sync endpoint uses `appSlug` to identify the app, so it cannot reliably match this request to the Zoom credential.

Concurrent initial webhooks can create duplicate credentials

The lookup at line 62 and the create here are separate, non-atomic operations. If two deliveries for the same user and app arrive before either creates its row, both observe no credential and insert one. This leaves duplicate credentials, after which consumers using `findFirst` may select an arbitrary copy.

This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Immediate cancellations still fill SendGrid's pending-cancellation limit

When `immediateDelete` is true, this sends the SendGrid cancel request immediately and returns without setting `cancelled=true`. Rescheduling uses this path, as do workflow/step deletion, so far-future sends remain in SendGrid's pending-cancellation queue until their scheduled dates—the limit of 100 that this PR is intended to avoid can still be reached. Once reached, later cancellations can fail and reminders may be sent. If the request fails, the error is swallowed and the cron has no `cancelled` flag to retry. These cancellations need to use the deferred cancellation flow or otherwise ensure they are cleaned up and retried.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the exact same bug in the `immediateDelete: true` path of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`: it cancels the email via SendGrid and returns without deleting the database record or setting `cancelled=true` and without calling the SendGrid DELETE API to clean up the batch, leaving orphaned records and uncleaned SendGrid batches.

One failed cancellation aborts the rest of the cron batch

The `try` covers the entire loop, so a single failed SendGrid request exits the loop and skips every later cancelled reminder in the batch. Those reminders remain pending at SendGrid; if one becomes due before the next cron run, the initial cleanup at lines 34–41 deletes its database row before it can be retried, and the email can be sent. Handle failures per reminder or ensure due cancelled reminders are processed before cleanup.

This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Mixed-case addresses bypass the guest email blocklist

Validation side effects count each signup attempt more than once

`BlockedEmail.should_block?` increments match statistics, but it is called from a validator, which can run multiple times for one operation. In particular, `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again; a matching address therefore increments `match_count` twice for one signup attempt. Keep validation side-effect-free and record a match once at the submission boundary.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments say the check method (should_block) has side effects: it updates match statistics during what should be a read-only check. The candidate gives a different consequence (double counting from repeated validation) rather than race conditions, but the underlying issue, side effects in a read/check method, is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Exact email lookup lets casing changes bypass the blocklist

This lookup compares the submitted address verbatim with the stored address, and signup does not normalize the email before validation. Because email domains are case-insensitive, a user can submit the same address with different domain casing (for example, `bad@SPAMCLUB.COM` instead of `bad@spamclub.com`) and avoid the blocklist match. Normalize both stored and submitted addresses before comparing them.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same flaw: the blocked email lookup is case-sensitive, so a user can bypass the blocklist by changing the casing of the address.

false_positives.candidate:
Concurrent matches can lose counter increments

The counter is updated with a read-modify-save sequence. If two signup validations load the same row before either saves, both can write the same incremented value, losing one match from `match_count`. Use an atomic database increment (and update the timestamp atomically) or lock the row.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
The small-action button no longer floats to the right

Making `.small-action` a flex container causes its button child to ignore the existing `float: right`. Since `.small-action-desc` has no flex-grow, the button can sit directly beside the message instead of at the far right, changing the placement of the action control. Give the description flexible space or push the button to the end with a flex-compatible rule.

The legacy flexbox fallback may not keep the panel right-aligned

For browsers that use the `-webkit-box` or `-moz-box` fallback but do not support modern flexbox, `margin-left: auto` does not provide the modern flex auto-margin behavior that pushes the panel to the right. The previous `float: right` has also been removed, so the panel can sit beside the title rather than at the right edge.

The old Firefox flexbox fallback omits its alignment property

`flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` for older Firefox, but `align-items()` does not emit the corresponding `-moz-box-align`. In browsers using that fallback, requested vertical alignment (such as the header's `center`) is ignored and the items use the old box model's default alignment. Add the matching legacy property or remove the fallback.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Website privacy restriction is bypassed by website_name

`website` is an untrusted attribute, so it is omitted for anonymous viewers of TL0 users when `restrict_user_fields?` applies. The newly serialized `website_name` is not in `untrusted_attributes`, and its inclusion method lacks the `?` used by the serializer's inclusion checks. It therefore still exposes the website host—and sometimes its path—in the user JSON, bypassing the existing privacy restriction.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly says the inclusion method lacks the `?` the serializer's inclusion checks rely on, which is the core point of the golden comment. Its main framing is a privacy bypass, but it identifies the same missing-? defect in include_website_name. It does not mention the string mutation issue, so the match is partial.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
RSS items with only a description abort feed polling

A standard RSS item commonly provides its body in `<description>` rather than `content`; when SimpleRSS has no `content` value, calling `.scrub` on it raises `NoMethodError`. That aborts the poll before later items are processed, and this job has retries disabled. Fall back to the item's description (and handle items with neither field).
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same bug: calling .scrub on a nil content when an RSS item has only a description raises an error. Both also recommend falling back to description.

false_positives.candidate:
Raw HTML imports bypass post sanitization

Posts imported from RSS are assigned `cook_method: raw_html`, so this branch stores the feed's HTML directly as `cooked` instead of passing it through the normal rendering and sanitization pipeline. Feed content is unescaped before import and is rendered as HTML, so a feed publisher can inject scripts or event handlers that execute on forum pages with the forum's origin and user privileges. Sanitize imported HTML before it is stored or rendered.

Remote fetches can follow redirects to internal addresses

The embed URL's hostname is checked before this fetch, but `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects without rechecking the destination. An allowed-host URL that redirects to loopback, a private network address, or cloud metadata can therefore make the server fetch internal resources; the response is then passed into the import path. Restrict redirect targets and reject private or otherwise non-public resolved addresses.

The iframe height attribute is assigned an invalid value

`HTMLIFrameElement.height` reflects an integer-pixel HTML attribute, but this assigns a value such as `500px`. Browsers can treat that as invalid and use the default iframe height instead, leaving the embed clipped even after receiving a resize message. Assign the numeric pixel value or set `iframe.style.height`.

The embed URL column truncates valid long URLs

A Rails `string` column defaults to `varchar(255)`, while valid embed URLs can exceed 255 characters, especially when they contain query parameters. Saving such an embed raises a database error inside the topic transaction, so the topic import is rolled back. Use a column type and index strategy that support the intended URL lengths.

The throttle key can be left without an expiration

`SETNX` and `EXPIRE` are separate Redis operations. If the process stops or the second command fails after `SETNX` succeeds, the key remains indefinitely; subsequent non-staff retrieval attempts then treat the URL as recently retrieved and never fetch it. Set the key and TTL atomically, or remove the key when expiration setup fails.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The second method definition overwrites the width/height form

Ruby does not overload methods by argument list, so this definition replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition immediately above it. Existing callers using the previously supported width/height arguments will now pass the height as `opts` or raise an argument error, breaking those callers. Use a single method that handles both forms or update all callers.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same problem. The downsize method is defined twice, and the second definition overrides the width/height version. That breaks existing callers that pass separate width and height arguments.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The client-side limit now ignores configured attachment sizes

This fixed 10 MB limit is applied to both images and attachments, bypassing the configured per-type limits. For example, installations that allow attachments larger than 10 MB will have valid uploads rejected in the browser; installations with a lower attachment limit will let users submit files the server then rejects. Keep attachment validation tied to its configured limit.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments say the hardcoded 10MB limit bypasses the configured per-type size settings, which lets client and server validation diverge. The candidate does not mention the 413 handler, but the core issue is the same.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsizing can permanently discard animation frames

When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, `OptimizedImage` uses its non-animated conversion path, which reads only `from[0]`. Because this call uses the same path for input and output, an oversized animated GIF is replaced with a still image and its remaining frames are lost. Thumbnail settings should not silently destroy animation in the uploaded file.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Unsubscribe does not mute users who are tracking or watching

When a user's notification level is `tracking` or `watching`, this branch lowers it only to `regular`. Regular topics can still send notifications for replies and mentions, so the page's promise to stop notifications is not met. Set the level to `muted` for every unsubscribe request, regardless of the starting level.

Saving the level directly lets auto-tracking undo the unsubscribe

This direct save bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which stamps `notifications_changed_at` and sets `notifications_reason_id` to `user_changed` when a notification level is explicitly changed. Email recipients can have a topic-user row with a nil reason; `update_last_read` treats that row as eligible for automatic tracking and can raise the level back to `tracking` after the user reads enough of the topic. Use the normal notification-level update path so the user's explicit preference is preserved.

The GET unsubscribe endpoint changes user state

This action is reached through a GET route but changes the current user's notification preference before returning the page. Because GET requests do not require a CSRF token, a cross-site link or navigation can trigger the change whenever the user has an active Discourse session. Keep GET read-only and require an explicit CSRF-protected action to apply the preference.

The route name does not match the added template path

This declares a top-level `topicUnsubscribe` route, whose conventional template lookup is for `topic-unsubscribe`; the added template is `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which corresponds to a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route. There is no explicit template-name override, so visiting this route will not render the unsubscribe page. Nest the route under `topic` or provide a template matching the declared route name.

false_negatives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The existing-URL update only works with BSD sed

`sed -i ''` uses BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU/Linux, when `.env` already contains `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`, this command treats the empty argument as a file operand and fails to update the value; because the script does not stop on that failure, it can still print that the file was updated. Use a portable in-place edit or branch on the platform.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same bug: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS-only syntax and fails on GNU/Linux. The candidate adds detail, but it describes the same underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Deleting cache leaves the displayed status stale

The delete mutation only invokes an optional `onSuccess` callback and does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. When no callback is provided, the mounted query retains the deleted cache’s `cacheUpdatedAt`, so the dropdown continues to report cached data and offer deletion after the operation succeeded. Invalidate or refetch the connected-calendars query after deletion.

Legacy cache rows are reported as updated at migration time

Adding this column with `DEFAULT NOW()` assigns the migration timestamp to every existing cache row. The UI presents `updatedAt` as the cache’s last-updated time, so all pre-existing caches appear freshly updated on deployment even when their contents are older. Backfill a timestamp derived from the existing cache metadata, or avoid presenting the migration-time value as the actual update time.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hour check ignores the event end time

`end` is calculated identically to `start`, so the check only verifies that the slot begins within a working-hour interval. A fixed host whose hours end at 10:00 can consequently be treated as available for a 09:30 slot lasting 60 minutes, even though the event ends at 10:30. Check the slot's actual end against the interval end.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: the end time is computed from the slot start time rather than the slot end time, so the working-hour check never looks at when the slot actually ends.

false_positives.candidate:
Date overrides bypass busy-time checks

When a slot falls within a date override, this returns `true` before the subsequent `busy.every` check. Existing bookings and calendar events are still reported in `busy`, so a host can be shown as available during an override despite already being booked, allowing a double booking. An override should replace regular working hours, not ignore busy times.

Multiple override windows reject each other

The `.find` callback returns a truthy value when the slot is outside the current override window, which immediately marks the slot unavailable without checking later windows. For example, with overrides 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a slot in either window is rejected because it falls outside the other one. Check whether the slot fits any window for that date instead.

Slots only need to overlap an override to be accepted

These checks reject slots wholly before or after an override, but accept any slot that overlaps it. For example, a 09:30–10:30 slot passes a 10:00–11:00 override even though it starts outside the host's availability. This can incorrectly count a fixed host as available for a slot generated from another host; require the entire slot to fit within the override.

Split working-hour windows make slots unavailable

This rejects a slot if `.find` finds any working-hour interval that does not contain it, rather than rejecting only when no interval contains it. With 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 hours, a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the second interval. Hosts with multiple windows on a day can therefore lose their availability.

Timezone conversion drops date changes across midnight

The timezone adjustment can move an override to the previous or next day, but this code keeps only its hour and minute and later anchors those to the unshifted invitee day. The active-override filter also selects overrides using the unshifted start date. For example, an override at 00:30 in UTC+5:30 maps to 19:00 on the prior UTC day, but is selected and placed on the original date for a UTC invitee. Availability near timezone day boundaries is therefore missing or shown on the wrong day.

Timezone test can pass when expected slots are missing

This assertion uses `toHaveTimeSlots`, whose implementation iterates the actual slots and compares each with the expected slot at that index. If the result contains only a matching prefix—for example, one of the four expected slots—the matcher still passes. The new timezone regression test therefore does not ensure that all expected slots are returned.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Increment retryCount atomically

Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value loaded before the SMS call. If two cron invocations process the same reminder concurrently, they can both read the same count and overwrite it with the same next value. The failed attempts are then counted as one, so the reminder can be retried more than twice instead of being removed at the intended limit. Use Prisma's atomic `increment` update in both failure paths.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same problem. retryCount is updated with the stale value reminder.retryCount + 1, so concurrent runs can lose increments. Both recommend Prisma's atomic increment, and both say it applies to both failure paths.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

false_positives.candidate:
Preserve or migrate the public `findMany` API

This change removes the service’s public `findMany` method and replaces it with a condition builder, but no production call sites are migrated in this PR. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany(...)` will no longer type-check, so the application cannot build until those callers are updated or a compatible method is retained.

Execute org and team authorization SQL in integration tests

The only database-backed query here uses user scope, which does not exercise the new `ANY(...)` array predicates. The org/team tests only compare `Prisma.Sql` fragments, so they will not catch invalid PostgreSQL array binding or incorrect authorization results when those predicates execute. Add database-backed queries covering org and team scopes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The minimum token schema does not capture arbitrary expiry fields

`z.string().toString()` is evaluated as a literal property name, not a wildcard key, and the same applies to the optional property on line 10. Consequently, normal fields such as `expires_in` or `expiry_date` are not validated or retained by this `z.object` (which strips unrecognized properties); depending on the computed keys, responses may also fail parsing. With credential syncing enabled, token refreshes across the affected apps therefore fail or lose their expiry data.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the computed keys z.string().toString() used as property names in minimumTokenResponseSchema being invalid or incorrect Zod usage, which breaks parsing. The candidate says the keys become literal property names rather than wildcard keys, so expiry fields get stripped and parsing may fail. That is the same underlying flaw, though the candidate describes the consequences somewhat differently from the golden comment's runtime error.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The SafeParse wrapper is saved as the Google credential key

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the result of `safeParse`, which has the shape `{ success, data }`, but this line stores that whole result as `credential.key` instead of its `.data`. After a token refresh, the next Google auth initialization parses this wrapper as a Google credential and fails, leaving the integration unusable.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: the safeParse wrapper is persisted as credential.key when the parsed .data should be stored.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Bigin sends a credential row ID as the user ID

The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is used as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`, the ID of the credential row, rather than the owning user's ID. The sync endpoint will look up the wrong user (or fail to find one), so Bigin token refreshes cannot reliably retrieve the correct user's credentials.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: `refreshOAuthTokens` is passed `credentialId` where the user ID is expected, which causes the sync to look up the wrong user. The candidate adds the Bigin context, but the underlying issue is identical.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The Salesforce connection uses the pre-refresh access token

The newly added code obtains and stores a refreshed token, but the connection is then constructed with `credentialKey.access_token`, which came from the original credential and was not updated with `accessTokenParsed.data`. When the original token is expired, Salesforce API calls therefore use the expired token despite the successful refresh.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. The jsforce connection is built with the stale credentialKey.access_token instead of the refreshed token, which causes authentication failures. The candidate does not mention instance_url, but the core issue is identical.

false_positives.candidate:
The new credential update references an unimported Prisma client

This file does not import or otherwise declare `prisma`, but the newly added refresh code calls `prisma.credential.update`. TypeScript compilation fails with an unresolved `prisma` name, preventing the app-store package or application from building.

Salesforce refresh bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint

This refresh path calls Salesforce directly instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`. When credential syncing is configured, Salesforce still refreshes against Cal.com's Salesforce app rather than the self-hosted platform's source of truth, so the advertised sync behavior does not work for Salesforce.

Webex rejects the documented minimal sync response

The sync endpoint is documented to return only an access token and expiry date, but the response is passed on to `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` at line 88, which also requires `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`. A response following the stated sync contract fails validation, so Webex refreshes fail and the integration cannot use synced credentials.

The synced Teams token is immediately treated as expired

The sync endpoint is expected to return an access token and expiry date, but the refresh handling later derives `expiry_date` solely from `expires_in` and overwrites it with `Date.now()` when `expires_in` is absent. The next `getToken` call sees that timestamp as expired and calls the sync endpoint again, causing repeated refresh requests and potentially rate-limiting the integration.

Zoom sync uses a different slug from the stored app credential

The refresh request identifies Zoom as `zoomvideo`, while Zoom credentials are stored with `appId: "zoom"` (as shown by the callback). The receiving sync endpoint uses `appSlug` to identify the app, so it cannot reliably match this request to the Zoom credential.

Concurrent initial webhooks can create duplicate credentials

The lookup at line 62 and the create here are separate, non-atomic operations. If two deliveries for the same user and app arrive before either creates its row, both observe no credential and insert one. This leaves duplicate credentials, after which consumers using `findFirst` may select an arbitrary copy.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Immediate cancellations still fill SendGrid's pending-cancellation limit

When `immediateDelete` is true, this sends the SendGrid cancel request immediately and returns without setting `cancelled=true`. Rescheduling uses this path, as do workflow/step deletion, so far-future sends remain in SendGrid's pending-cancellation queue until their scheduled dates—the limit of 100 that this PR is intended to avoid can still be reached. Once reached, later cancellations can fail and reminders may be sent. If the request fails, the error is swallowed and the cron has no `cancelled` flag to retry. These cancellations need to use the deferred cancellation flow or otherwise ensure they are cleaned up and retried.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the immediateDelete=true path: it sends the cancel and returns without updating the reminder record, so it is inconsistent with the deferred path. The golden comment's concern is that the WorkflowReminder DB record is never deleted, leaving orphaned entries, and that the DELETE call is omitted. The candidate's concern is that cancelled is not set, so the SendGrid pending-cancellation limit can still fill and failed requests are not retried. They overlap on the missing DB update, but the candidate frames it as a SendGrid limit and retry problem rather than orphaned records. That makes this a partial match.

false_positives.candidate:
One failed cancellation aborts the rest of the cron batch

The `try` covers the entire loop, so a single failed SendGrid request exits the loop and skips every later cancelled reminder in the batch. Those reminders remain pending at SendGrid; if one becomes due before the next cron run, the initial cleanup at lines 34–41 deletes its database row before it can be retried, and the email can be sent. Handle failures per reminder or ensure due cancelled reminders are processed before cleanup.

true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bypass: the blocklist performs an exact/case-sensitive email comparison, so changing the casing of a blocked address avoids the match. The candidate's domain-casing example is a specific instance of the broader case-sensitivity issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Concurrent matches can lose counter increments

The counter is updated with a read-modify-save sequence. If two signup validations load the same row before either saves, both can write the same incremented value, losing one match from `match_count`. Use an atomic database increment (and update the timestamp atomically) or lock the row.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

For browsers that use the `-webkit-box` or `-moz-box` fallback but do not support modern flexbox, `margin-left: auto` does not provide the modern flex auto-margin behavior that pushes the panel to the right. The previous `float: right` has also been removed, so the panel can sit beside the title rather than at the right edge.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same regression: removing the float-based right alignment for the header panel means margin-left:auto no longer guarantees right alignment outside modern flexbox, so the panel loses its right-edge placement.

false_positives.candidate:
The small-action button no longer floats to the right

Making `.small-action` a flex container causes its button child to ignore the existing `float: right`. Since `.small-action-desc` has no flex-grow, the button can sit directly beside the message instead of at the far right, changing the placement of the action control. Give the description flexible space or push the button to the end with a flex-compatible rule.

The old Firefox flexbox fallback omits its alignment property

`flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` for older Firefox, but `align-items()` does not emit the corresponding `-moz-box-align`. true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Website privacy restriction is bypassed by website_name

`website` is an untrusted attribute, so it is omitted for anonymous viewers of TL0 users when `restrict_user_fields?` applies. The newly serialized `website_name` is not in `untrusted_attributes`, and its inclusion method lacks the `?` used by the serializer's inclusion checks. It therefore still exposes the website host—and sometimes its path—in the user JSON, bypassing the existing privacy restriction.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same core bug: include_website_name lacks the required '?' suffix, so the serializer's conditional inclusion check doesn't apply and website_name is serialized when it shouldn't be. The candidate frames the consequence as a privacy bypass (exposing the website host), which aligns with the golden's point that the attribute isn't conditionally included as intended. The candidate omits the secondary string-concatenation concern, but the underlying issue matches.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

A standard RSS item commonly provides its body in `<description>` rather than `content`; when SimpleRSS has no `content` value, calling `.scrub` on it raises `NoMethodError`. That aborts the poll before later items are processed, and this job has retries disabled. Fall back to the item's description (and handle items with neither field).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: RSS items may lack content, so calling scrub on i.content raises NoMethodError and aborts polling. Both recommend falling back to description (candidate also notes handling neither field).

false_positives.candidate:
Raw HTML imports bypass post sanitization

Posts imported from RSS are assigned `cook_method: raw_html`, so this branch stores the feed's HTML directly as `cooked` instead of passing it through the normal rendering and sanitization pipeline. Feed content is unescaped before import and is rendered as HTML, so a feed publisher can inject scripts or event handlers that execute on forum pages with the forum's origin and user privileges. Sanitize imported HTML before it is stored or rendered.

Remote fetches can follow redirects to internal addresses

The embed URL's hostname is checked before this fetch, but `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects without rechecking the destination. An allowed-host URL that redirects to loopback, a private network address, or cloud metadata can therefore make the server fetch internal resources; the response is then passed into the import path. Restrict redirect targets and reject private or otherwise non-public resolved addresses.

The iframe height attribute is assigned an invalid value

`HTMLIFrameElement.height` reflects an integer-pixel HTML attribute, but this assigns a value such as `500px`. Browsers can treat that as invalid and use the default iframe height instead, leaving the embed clipped even after receiving a resize message. Assign the numeric pixel value or set `iframe.style.height`.

The embed URL column truncates valid long URLs

A Rails `string` column defaults to `varchar(255)`, while valid embed URLs can exceed 255 characters, especially when they contain query parameters. Saving such an embed raises a database error inside the topic transaction, so the topic import is rolled back. Use a column type and index strategy that support the intended URL lengths.

The throttle key can be left without an expiration

`SETNX` and `EXPIRE` are separate Redis operations. If the process stops or the second command fails after `SETNX` succeeds, the key remains indefinitely; subsequent non-staff retrieval attempts then treat the URL as recently retrieved and never fetch it. Set the key and TTL atomically, or remove the key when expiration setup fails.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

Unsubscribe does not mute users who are tracking or watching

When a user's notification level is `tracking` or `watching`, this branch lowers it only to `regular`. true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:

`end` is calculated identically to `start`, so the check only verifies that the slot begins within a working-hour interval. A fixed host whose hours end at 10:00 can consequently be treated as available for a 09:30 slot lasting 60 minutes, even though the event ends at 10:30. Check the slot's actual end against the interval end.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the working-hour availability check computes the slot end identically to the start (using slotStartTime), so it only validates the start and ignores the actual event end time.

false_positives.candidate:
Date overrides bypass busy-time checks

When a slot falls within a date override, this returns `true` before the subsequent `busy.every` check. Existing bookings and calendar events are still reported in `busy`, so a host can be shown as available during an override despite already being booked, allowing a double booking. An override should replace regular working hours, not ignore busy times.

Multiple override windows reject each other

The `.find` callback returns a truthy value when the slot is outside the current override window, which immediately marks the slot unavailable without checking later windows. For example, with overrides 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a slot in either window is rejected because it falls outside the other one. Check whether the slot fits any window for that date instead.

Split working-hour windows make slots unavailable

This rejects a slot if `.find` finds any working-hour interval that does not contain it, rather than rejecting only when no interval contains it. With 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 hours, a 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the second interval. Hosts with multiple windows on a day can therefore lose their availability.

Timezone conversion drops date changes across midnight

The timezone adjustment can move an override to the previous or next day, but this code keeps only its hour and minute and later anchors those to the unshifted invitee day. The active-override filter also selects overrides using the unshifted start date. For example, an override at 00:30 in UTC+5:30 maps to 19:00 on the prior UTC day, but is selected and placed on the original date for a UTC invitee. Availability near timezone day boundaries is therefore missing or shown on the wrong day.

Timezone test can pass when expected slots are missing

This assertion uses `toHaveTimeSlots`, whose implementation iterates the actual slots and compares each with the expected slot at that index. If the result contains only a matching prefix—for example, one of the four expected slots—the matcher still passes. The new timezone regression test therefore does not ensure that all expected slots are returned.

Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value loaded before the SMS call. The failed attempts are then counted as one, so the reminder can be retried more than twice instead of being removed at the intended limit. Use Prisma's atomic `increment` update in both failure paths.

With credential syncing enabled, token refreshes across the affected apps therefore fail or lose their expiry data.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse wrapper ({success, data, error}), but the code persists the wrapper as credential.key instead of the parsed token payload (.data), causing subsequent Google auth initialization to fail.
